1. Meaning of Women Empowerment

Women Empowerment is the process of enabling women to enjoy:

  • Equal rights.
  • Equal opportunities.
  • Equal access to resources.
  • Equal participation in social, economic and political life.

It seeks to enable women to:

  • Make independent decisions.
  • Exercise constitutional and legal rights.
  • Live with dignity, equality and security.
  • Participate fully in nation-building.
📌 Must-Memorise

Women Empowerment → Rights + Opportunities + Resources + Participation + Independence

2. Empowerment Is More Than Welfare

Women empowerment is not merely:

  • Providing benefits.
  • Providing temporary assistance.

It creates conditions in which women can:

  • Exercise rights independently.
  • Become self-reliant.
  • Participate in decision-making.
  • Control economic and social choices.

3. Need for Women Empowerment

Historically, women have faced inequalities in:

  • Education.
  • Employment.
  • Property rights.
  • Political participation.
  • Decision-making.
  • Healthcare.
  • Social status.
  • Access to resources.

4. Objectives

The major objectives are:

  • Achieve gender equality.
  • Eliminate discrimination.
  • Ensure equal opportunities.
  • Improve education.
  • Promote economic independence.
  • Increase political participation.
  • Improve health and nutrition.
  • Prevent violence against women.
  • Strengthen legal protection.
  • Ensure equal participation in national development.

5. Importance

Women empowerment contributes to:

  • Social justice.
  • Inclusive development.
  • Economic growth.
  • Poverty reduction.
  • Better family welfare.
  • Improved education.
  • Better health outcomes.
  • Democratic participation.
  • Sustainable development.
  • National progress.

6. Constitutional Vision

The Constitution guarantees:

  • Justice.
  • Liberty.
  • Equality.
  • Dignity.

These ideals apply equally to:

  • Women.
  • Men.

7. Constitutional Sources of Women Empowerment

The constitutional framework includes:

  • Preamble.
  • Fundamental Rights.
  • Directive Principles of State Policy.
  • Fundamental Duties.
  • Special provisions for women.
  • Reservation in Local Self-Government.
  • Reservation in legislatures under the 106th Amendment.

8. Preamble

The Preamble secures:

  • Justice.
  • Liberty.
  • Equality.
  • Fraternity.

Equality of:

  • Status.
  • Opportunity

forms an important constitutional foundation for gender justice.

9. Article 14

Article 14 guarantees:

  • Equality Before Law.

Women and men possess:

  • Equal legal status before law.

38. Meaning of Gender Equality

Gender equality means equal:

  • Rights.
  • Opportunities.
  • Responsibilities.
  • Access to resources.
  • Participation in decision-making

for women and men.

39. Equality vs Equity

Equality:

  • Same legal rights and opportunities.

Equity:

  • Fair support based on differing needs and disadvantages.
  • Helps achieve substantive equality.

40. Women Empowerment vs Women Welfare

Women Empowerment:

  • Rights-based.
  • Self-reliance.
  • Long-term transformation.

Women Welfare:

  • Assistance-based.
  • Support and benefits.
  • Immediate relief.

Rapid Revision — TNPSC Most Expected

What is Women Empowerment? → Process of enabling women to enjoy equal rights, opportunities, resources and participation.

Is Women Empowerment the same as Women Welfare? → No.

What is the difference? → Empowerment builds independence and rights; welfare mainly provides assistance.

Which constitutional ideals form the foundation of women empowerment? → Justice, Liberty, Equality and Dignity.

Which Article guarantees Equality Before Law? → Article 14.

Which Article prohibits discrimination based on sex? → Article 15.

Which Article permits special provisions for women and children? → Article 15(3).

Are special provisions for women unconstitutional discrimination? → No.

Which Article provides equality of opportunity in public employment? → Article 16.

Which Article protects dignity, bodily integrity and reproductive autonomy through judicial interpretation? → Article 21.

Which Article prohibits human trafficking? → Article 23.

Which Article provides equal right to adequate livelihood? → Article 39(a).

Which Article provides Equal Pay for Equal Work? → Article 39(d).

Which Article protects health and strength of workers? → Article 39(e).

Which Article deals with maternity relief? → Article 42.

Which Article directs the State towards a Uniform Civil Code? → Article 44.

Which Fundamental Duty specifically concerns women's dignity? → Article 51A(e).

What does Article 51A(e) require? → Renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

Which Article reserves seats for women in Panchayats? → Article 243D.

What is the constitutional minimum? → Not less than one-third.

Which Article reserves seats for women in Municipalities? → Article 243T.

What minimum does it provide? → Not less than one-third.

Can States provide 50% reservation? → Yes, through State legislation; the attachment notes several States including Tamil Nadu do so.

Which Amendment provides women's reservation in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies? → Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.

What is its popular name? → Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam.

Which Article provides women's reservation in Lok Sabha? → Article 330A.

Which Article provides women's reservation in State Assemblies? → Article 332A.

How much reservation? → One-third of seats.

When will it take effect according to the attachment? → After the first Census following commencement of the Amendment and subsequent delimitation.

Which Act protects women from domestic violence? → Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

What types of abuse does it cover? → Physical, sexual, verbal, emotional and economic abuse.

Which Act prohibits dowry? → Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

Which law deals with workplace sexual harassment? → Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013.

What workplace body handles complaints? → Internal Committee.

Which body handles specified cases where an IC is unavailable/not required? → Local Committee.

Which law prohibits child marriage? → Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.

What marriage ages are stated in the source? → Women 18; men 21.

Which law provides maternity protection? → Maternity Benefit Act, 1961.

Which law granted daughters equal coparcenary rights? → Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005.

Which Act prohibits sex selection? → PCPNDT Act, 1994.

Which institution is the national statutory body for women's rights? → National Commission for Women.

Which law established NCW? → National Commission for Women Act, 1990.

When did NCW become functional? → 1992.

Is NCW constitutional or statutory? → Statutory.

What is its composition? → Chairperson, five Members and Member-Secretary.

What are major NCW functions? → Review safeguards, investigate complaints, recommend reforms, legal awareness and advise Government.

Which scheme was launched in 2015 for the girl child? → Beti Bachao Beti Padhao.

What are its major objectives? → Prevent gender-biased sex selection, improve child sex ratio, promote girls' education and empowerment.

What is Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana? → Small-savings scheme for girl children.

What is PMMVY? → Maternity-benefit and maternal-health support scheme.

What does One Stop Centre provide? → Medical, police, legal, counselling and temporary-shelter support for women affected by violence.

What is Mission Shakti? → Umbrella programme for women's safety, security and empowerment.

What is Economic Empowerment? → Financial independence through income, property, credit and economic participation.

What is the role of SHGs? → Savings, credit, entrepreneurship and livelihood support.

What is Educational Empowerment? → Equal access to school, higher, vocational and professional education.

What is Political Empowerment? → Equal participation in elections, public office and decision-making.

What is Social Empowerment? → Equal dignity, social status, safety and opportunity.

What is Digital Empowerment? → Access to digital education, finance, e-governance and employment opportunities.

What are major challenges? → Discrimination, stereotypes, violence, economic inequality, educational disadvantage, health problems, political under-representation and digital divide.

Which case is associated with discriminatory employment conditions for air hostesses? → Air India v. Nergesh Meerza, 1981.

Which case strengthened inheritance rights of Syrian Christian women? → Mary Roy v. State of Kerala, 1986.

Which case laid down workplace sexual-harassment guidelines? → Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan, 1997.

Which Articles were linked to Vishaka in the attachment? → Articles 14, 15, 19(1)(g) and 21.

Which case strengthened mother's guardianship rights? → Githa Hariharan v. RBI, 1999.

Which case extended maternity protection to casual workers? → MCD v. Female Workers, 2000.

Which case protected a woman's freedom to marry a person of her choice? → Lata Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh, 2006.

Which case rejected paternalistic restrictions on women's employment? → Anuj Garg v. Hotel Association of India, 2008.

Which case recognised reproductive autonomy under Article 21? → Suchita Srivastava v. Chandigarh Administration, 2009.

Which case broadened Domestic Violence Act protection beyond an “adult male person”? → Hiral P. Harsora v. Kusum Harsora, 2016.

Which case invalidated Instant Triple Talaq? → Shayara Bano v. Union of India, 2017.

Which case recognised Privacy as a Fundamental Right? → K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, 2017.

Which case struck down the adultery offence under former Section 497 IPC? → Joseph Shine v. Union of India, 2018.

Which case dealt with Permanent Commission for women Army officers? → Secretary, Ministry of Defence v. Babita Puniya, 2020.

Which case held a daughter becomes a coparcener by birth? → Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma, 2020.

Which case recognised Indirect Discrimination? → Lt. Col. Nitisha v. Union of India, 2021.

Which 2022 case strengthened reproductive rights of unmarried women? → X v. Principal Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department.

What is the core TNPSC memory line? → Article 14 gives equality, Article 15(3) permits special provisions, Article 39(d) provides Equal Pay, Article 42 gives maternity protection, Article 51A(e) protects women's dignity, Articles 243D and 243T provide Local Body reservation, and Articles 330A and 332A provide legislative reservation under the 106th Amendment.
